name: Menachem
overview: Menachem was a male king of Israel, known primarily for his reign as recorded in 2 Kings 15:14. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his role as king marks him as a significant figure in the northern kingdom's history. There are no additional personal notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Menachem means 'comforter' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name given to him. This meaning may suggest a role or hope for relief or support during his time, although the name was not explicitly given by God according to the record in 2 Kings 15:14.
familyAndRelationships: Menachem was the father of Gadi, as explicitly stated in Scripture. He was also the son of Pekahiah, inferred from the biblical text. His death was caused by Shallum, who killed him, indicating a violent end to his reign.
scriptureSignificance: Menachem's significance lies in his kingship over Israel during a turbulent period, as documented in 2 Kings 15:14. His lineage connects him to Pekahiah, and his violent death at the hands of Shallum highlights the instability and conflict within the northern kingdom. His reign contributes to the broader biblical narrative of Israel's monarchy and its challenges.
